arxiv-2102-03194.title: Detecting Atmospheric Molecules of Temperate Terrestrial Exoplanets using High-Resolution Spectroscopy in the Mid Infrared Domain
arxiv-2102-03194.creator: Yuka Fujii, Taro Matsuo
arxiv-2102-03194.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yuka Fujii, Taro Matsuo. Motivated by the development of high-dispersion spectrographs in the mid-infrared (MIR) range, we study their application to the atmospheric characterization of nearby non-transiting temperate terrestrial planets around M-type stars. We examine the detectability of CO 2 , H 2 O, N 2 O, and O 3 in high-resolution planetary thermal emission spectra at 12-18 μ \mu m assuming an Earth-like profile and a simplified thermal structure.

arxiv-2210-07985.title: Simulating scalar field theories on quantum computers with limited resources
arxiv-2210-07985.creator: Andy C. Y. Li, Alexandru Macridin, Stephen Mrenna, Panagiotis Spentzouris
arxiv-2210-07985.description: Abstract We present a quantum algorithm for implementing ϕ 4 \phi^{4} lattice scalar field theory on qubit computers. The field is represented in the discretized field amplitude basis. The number of qubits and elementary gates required by the implementation of the evolution operator is proportional to the lattice size.

arxiv-2211-01454.title: Speeding up NAS with Adaptive Subset Selection
arxiv-2211-01454.creator: Vishak Prasad C, Colin White, Paarth Jain, Sibasis Nayak, Ganesh Ramakrishnan
arxiv-2211-01454.description: Abstract A majority of recent developments in neural architecture search (NAS) have been aimed at decreasing the computational cost of various techniques without affecting their final performance. Towards this goal, several low-fidelity and performance prediction methods have been considered, including those that train only on subsets of the training data.

arxiv-2306-03480.title: Generative Modeling of Labeled Graphs under Data Scarcity
arxiv-2306-03480.creator: Sahil Manchanda, Shubham Gupta, Sayan Ranu, Srikanta Bedathur, Department of Computer Science, Engineering
arxiv-2306-03480.description: Abstract Deep graph generative modeling has gained enormous attraction in recent years due to its impressive ability to directly learn the underlying hidden graph distribution. Despite their initial success, these techniques, like many of the existing deep generative methods, require a large number of training samples to learn a good model.

arxiv-2310-14984.title: My Lockdown Escape: Sparking Self-Empathy in the Context of the Covid-19 Pandemic
arxiv-2310-14984.creator: Andrea Tocchetti, Silvia Maria Talenti, Marco Brambilla
arxiv-2310-14984.description: Abstract During the Covid-19 pandemic, research communities focused on collecting and understanding people’s behaviours and feelings to study and tackle the pandemic indirect effects. Despite its consequences are slowly starting to fade away, such an interest is still alive. In this article, we propose a hybrid, gamified, story-driven data collection approach to spark self-empathy, hence resurfacing people’s past feelings.

arxiv-2402-13194.title: Quantum Wiretap Channel Coding Assisted by Noisy Correlation
arxiv-2402-13194.creator: Minglai Cai 1, Andreas Winter 1,2,3,4
arxiv-2402-13194.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Minglai Cai 1, Andreas Winter 1,2,3,4. We consider the private classical capacity of a quantum wiretap channel, where the users (sender Alice, receiver Bob, and eavesdropper Eve) have access to the resource of a shared quantum state, additionally to their channel inputs and outputs. An extreme case is maximal entanglement or a secret key between Alice and Bob, both of which would allow for one-time padding the message. But here both the wiretap channel and the shared state are general.

arxiv-2503-02497.title: A PennyLane-Centric Dataset to Enhance LLM-based Quantum Code Generation using RAG
arxiv-2503-02497.creator: Abdul Basit 1 , Nouhaila Innan 1,2 , Muhammad Haider Asif 1,2 , Minghao Shao 1 , Muhammad Kashif 1,2 , Alberto Marchisio 1,2 , Muhammad Shafique 1,2
arxiv-2503-02497.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) offer powerful capabilities in code generation, natural language understanding, and domain-specific reasoning. Their application to quantum software development remains limited, in part because of the lack of high-quality datasets both for LLM training and as dependable knowledge sources.

arxiv-2508-11902.title: A Sobel-Gradient MLP Baseline for Handwritten Character Recognition
arxiv-2508-11902.creator: Azam Nouri
arxiv-2508-11902.description: Abstract We revisit the classical Sobel operator to ask a simple question: Are first-order edge maps sufficient to drive an all-dense MLP for handwritten character recognition(HCR), as an alternative to convolutional neural networks (CNNs)? Using only horizontal and vertical Sobel derivatives as input, we train a multilayer perceptron (MLP) on MNIST and EMNIST Letters.

pmc-12488420.title: Improving the teaching of “correlation does not equal causation” in Introductory Psychology
pmc-12488420.creator: Courtney Stevens, Melissa R. Witkow, Jason Isbell
pmc-12488420.description: “Correlation does not equal causation” is perhaps the most familiar phrase to any student or instructor in an Introductory Psychology class. While short and pithy, we argue that this phrase and its variants can lead to confusion among students, who may incorrectly interpret it to mean that “correlation cannot mean causation.

pmc-12523103.title: The significant prognostic value of the hemoglobin, albumin, lymphocyte, and platelet (HALP) score in digestive system cancers: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12523103.creator: Caihua Qian, Jingting Liu, Chunyan Meng, Jun Cheng, Bo Wu, Jianhua Liao
pmc-12523103.description: BackgroundDigestive system cancers are a major global health burden, necessitating reliable and cost-effective prognostic biomarkers for clinical decision-making. The hemoglobin, albumin, lymphocyte, and platelet (HALP) score, an integrated immune-nutrition marker, has emerged as a potential prognostic tool in various malignancies. This meta-analysis evaluated the prognostic value of the HALP score in patients with digestive system cancers.

pmc-12603647.title: ﻿The psyllid genus Ciriacremum (Hemiptera, Psyllidae) in Brazil
pmc-12603647.creator: Daniel Burckhardt, Dalva Luiz de Queiroz
pmc-12603647.description: ﻿AbstractCiriacremum is a genus of Ciriacreminae (Hemiptera, Sternorrhyncha, Psylloidea, Psyllidae) comprising 26 validly described species in the Afrotropical realm and only one in the Neotropics. Here we add four new species from Brazil, which are named and diagnosed, including illustrations and an identification key for adults: Ciriacremum lanceolatumsp. nov. (from Mato Grosso), C. maederaesp. nov. (from Amazonas), C. pollicigerumsp. nov.

pmc-13054477.title: Facile sonochemical route to sponge-like porous AgCl/malachite for enhanced photocatalytic performance and stability
pmc-13054477.creator: Hongbo He, Simin Zhong, Wanting Xiao, Jianhong Jiang, Yijun Guo, Siyao Tan, Shiya He, Midong Shi, Erjun Zhang, Bin Deng
pmc-13054477.description: Addressing the persistent challenges of photochemical corrosion and poor stability in silver-based photocatalysts, this study proposes a sonochemical synthesis strategy to construct sponge-like porous AgCl/Malachite heterojunction composites. The as-prepared material exhibits outstanding photocatalytic activity and cycling stability toward methyl orange (MO). Under light irradiation, the composite achieves a degradation efficiency of 92.

pmc-13241693.title: Knowledge, Attitude, and Perception of Medical Students Toward AI‐Based Learning: A Cross‐Sectional Study
pmc-13241693.creator: Danyal Khan, Muhammad Dawood, Ihtiram Ullah, Husna Irfan Thalib, Sadia Yasir Khan, Farasat Maheen, Mable Pereira
pmc-13241693.description: BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming healthcare delivery and medical education. Despite its growing global presence, little is known about the knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions (KAP) of medical students in Pakistan regarding AI‐based learning. Understanding these factors is essential for guiding curriculum development and preparing future physicians for an AI‐driven health system.

pmc-13494543.title: Optimizing microhomology-based genome editing by engineering DNA polymerase θ for improved efficiency and reduced on-target indels
pmc-13494543.creator: Wanyi Wang, Meng Zhou, Tianshan Ji, Qin Jiang, Jinyi Zhao, Zimeng Xu, Ruofei Liu, Yining Luo, Feng Han, Le Cong, Lei Fan, Chen Chen, Chengkun Wang
pmc-13494543.description: SummaryPrecise genome editing through targeted DNA insertion is critical for gene therapy and biomedical research. While existing methods rely on homology-directed repair (HDR), this process suffers from low efficiency in non-dividing cells. Microhomology-mediated repair provides an alternative but remains intrinsically inefficient.

pmc-13583180.title: Predicting Hospital Length of Stay in Orthopedic Trauma Patients Using Fracture‐Specific Machine Learning Models: A Multicenter Retrospective Prediction‐Modeling Study
pmc-13583180.creator: Parviz Marouzi, Amir Ahmadi, Seyyedeh Fatemeh Mousavi Baigi, Mohammad H. Ebrahimzadeh, Seyyed Mohammad Tabatabaei, Masoumeh Sarbaz, Khalil Kimiafar
pmc-13583180.description: Background and AimsHospital length of stay (LOS) is a key indicator for resource allocation, bed management, and discharge planning in orthopedic trauma care. Given the substantial heterogeneity of LOS across fracture types and the limitations of conventional approaches, this study aimed to develop and validate fracture‐specific machine learning models for predicting short vs. long hospital stay.
